title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
AbstractSystematic screening for cancer genes (CGs) is still a central goal in precision oncology, yet integrating sparse and spatially dispersed oncogenic signals to identify testable candidates remains challenging. Here we present CGMap, an interpretable graph-learning framework that uses a width-oriented parallel architecture to prioritize potential CGs from biomolecular networks and trace mechanistic cues. By constructing distance-resolved channels, CGMap localizes spatially dispersed CG signals across multiple topological scales while avoiding representation homogenization. A global diffusion module quantifies gene cooperativity along pathway contexts and yields traceable virtual interactions that map predictions to potential regulatory hypotheses, providing intrinsic interpretability for model decisions. Across multiple biomolecular networks in a pan-cancer setting, CGMap analysed 12,022 genes, consistently outperformed existing methods while remaining computationally efficient and prioritized 70 reliable candidates, including those previously unannotated in established databases. Importantly, the prioritized candidates were associated with the suppression of tumour-related phenotypes, including reduced cell proliferation, migration and invasion, along with a shift of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related features toward a non-mesenchymal state, as supported by parallel loss-of-function assays across cancer and non-malignant cell lines.

Data availability

The datasets supporting the findings of this study are available and a detailed list can be accessed via GitHub: https://github.com/Incendio1/CGMap. The precomputed data generated for CGMap have been deposited in Zenodo under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22941133 (ref. 98). Downstream benchmarks for CG backgrounds are primarily from the original paper, and other graph representation learning benchmarks are available at https://github.com/pyg-team/pytorch_geometric. Additionally, the Optuna v.4 framework for automated hyperparameter search can be found at https://github.com/optuna/optuna. The CCG cohort was taken from NCG7.2, http://network-cancer-genes.org/candidate_drivers.php. Data sources used to validate CGs include GEPIA2 (http://gepia2.cancer-pku.cn), TIMER 2.0 (https://compbio.cn/timer2/) and CancerSEA (http://biocc.hrbmu.edu.cn/CancerSEA). Data preparation and preprocessing refer to https://github.com/schulter/EMOGI and https://github.com/NWPU-903PR/HGDC/tree/master.
Code availability

The source code of CGMap is available in GitHub at https://github.com/Incendio1/CGMap and has been archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22949247 (ref. 99).
